sections.title: Introduction

blocks.text: Special Leave Petition is a petition filed before the Supreme Court of India seeking special permission to appeal against a judgment, decree, determination, sentence or order passed by a court or tribunal.

It matters because SLP is not a routine appeal. The Supreme Court exercises discretionary jurisdiction under Article 136 and generally looks for serious legal error, miscarriage of justice, substantial question, perversity, jurisdictional error, violation of natural justice or grave injustice.

This service is relevant for parties affected by High Court orders, tribunal orders, appellate orders, civil judgments, criminal judgments, family-law orders, property disputes, commercial matters, arbitration-related orders, tax matters, service matters, consumer orders, regulatory orders and urgent stay-related matters.

sections.title: Quick Answer

blocks.text: Special Leave Petition is not a licence. It is a discretionary constitutional remedy before the Supreme Court under Article 136.
It is governed by the Constitution of India, Supreme Court Rules, 2013, limitation principles, Supreme Court practice, subject-specific laws and the impugned order being challenged.

It is not mandatory in every case. It is used when a party seeks Supreme Court intervention against an order of a court or tribunal and the matter has sufficient legal merit for discretionary consideration.

sections.title: Overview

blocks.text: In simple terms…
Special Leave Petition means asking the Supreme Court: “Please grant me special permission to appeal against this order because serious legal injustice has occurred.”
The Court first decides whether leave should be granted. If leave is granted, the matter proceeds as an appeal.
From a compliance perspective…

A Special Leave Petition requires careful review of the impugned order, limitation, certified copy, prior proceedings, pleadings, annexures, question of law, grounds, interim relief, caveat status, delay condonation, court fee, affidavit, vakalatnama, index, synopsis, list of dates, paper-book format and Supreme Court filing defects.

From a risk perspective, SLP should not be filed as a routine “last try.” Weak grounds, factual re-argument, incomplete annexures, wrong limitation calculation, non-disclosure of material facts, poor question framing or defective filing can lead to dismissal, delay or loss of urgent stay opportunity.

faqs.q: What is Special Leave Petition?
faqs.a: Special Leave Petition is a petition filed before the Supreme Court seeking permission to appeal against an order or judgment of a court or tribunal.

faqs.q: Is Special Leave Petition a licence?
faqs.a: No. It is not a licence. It is a discretionary constitutional remedy under Article 136.

faqs.q: Which Article governs SLP?
faqs.a: Article 136 of the Constitution of India governs Special Leave Petition.

faqs.q: Is SLP an appeal as of right?
faqs.a: No. SLP is not an appeal as of right. The Supreme Court must first grant leave.

faqs.q: Can SLP be filed against High Court order?
faqs.a: Yes. SLP is commonly filed against High Court judgments or orders, subject to maintainability and merits.

faqs.q: Can SLP be filed against tribunal order?
faqs.a: Yes. Article 136 covers orders of courts and tribunals, subject to constitutional and legal limitations.

faqs.q: Can SLP be filed in criminal matters?
faqs.a: Yes. Criminal SLP may be filed in appropriate cases involving serious legal error, miscarriage of justice, conviction, acquittal, bail or procedural issues.

faqs.q: What is the limitation for SLP?
faqs.a: Generally, SLP is filed within 90 days from the impugned order, or 60 days from refusal of certificate of fitness, subject to applicable rules and condonation principles.

faqs.q: Can delay be condoned?
faqs.a: Delay may be condoned if sufficient cause is shown. Condonation is not automatic.

faqs.q: Does filing SLP automatically stay the order?
faqs.a: No. A separate stay or interim relief application is required.

faqs.q: What is leave stage?
faqs.a: Leave stage is where the Supreme Court decides whether the matter deserves to proceed as an appeal.

faqs.q: What happens if leave is granted?
faqs.a: If leave is granted, the SLP becomes an appeal and proceeds to the appeal stage.

faqs.q: What happens if SLP is dismissed at admission?
faqs.a: If dismissed at admission, leave is refused and the impugned order generally remains undisturbed, subject to the exact order passed.

faqs.q: What documents are required for SLP?
faqs.a: Impugned order, certified copy, lower court record, pleadings, annexures, synopsis, list of dates, affidavit, vakalatnama, limitation chart and interim application documents are commonly required.

faqs.q: Is certified copy required?
faqs.a: Certified copy is generally important for filing and limitation. Exemption strategy may be reviewed in urgent cases.

faqs.q: Can fresh evidence be filed in SLP?
faqs.a: Supreme Court generally considers the record below. Additional documents require strong justification and proper application.

faqs.q: Can SLP be filed without Advocate-on-Record?
faqs.a: Supreme Court filing generally requires Advocate-on-Record coordination, unless party-in-person route is permitted under court rules.

faqs.q: What is AOR?
faqs.a: AOR means Advocate-on-Record, an advocate authorised to file and act in Supreme Court matters.

faqs.q: Can caveat be filed in SLP?
faqs.a: Yes. Respondents may file caveat so that no ex-parte order is passed without hearing them.

faqs.q: Can SLP be filed after review petition?
faqs.a: It depends on facts, limitation and order history. Review vs SLP sequencing should be carefully planned.

faqs.q: Can SLP be filed directly without appeal?
faqs.a: Sometimes yes, but if a statutory appeal or alternate remedy exists, maintainability and strategy must be reviewed.

faqs.q: Can SLP be filed against interim order?
faqs.a: Yes, in exceptional cases, but Supreme Court interference in interim orders is limited and fact-specific.

faqs.q: Can Supreme Court modify or remand the matter?
faqs.a: Yes. Depending on the case, the Court may dismiss, issue notice, grant stay, set aside, modify, remand or pass other appropriate orders.

faqs.q: What is the biggest mistake in SLP filing?
faqs.a: The biggest mistake is treating SLP as a routine appeal and filing without strong legal grounds, limitation discipline, certified copy and complete record.
